    def _build_observer(self):
        template = (
            "def observe(state):\n"
            "    {svars} = state\n"
            "    lfp = y1 - y2 - y3\n"
            "    return np.array([{voi_names}])"
        )
        svars = ",".join(self.state_variables)
        if len(self.state_variables) == 1:
            svars += ","
        code = template.format(
            svars=svars, voi_names=",".join(self.variables_of_interest)
        )
        # the namespace dfun runs in, plus this model's parameters
        namespace = {**globals(), **self.__dict__}
        self.log.debug("building observer with code:\n%s", code)
        exec(code, namespace)
        self.observe = namespace["observe"]
        self.observe.code = code

    def dfun(self, state_variables, coupling, local_coupling=0):

        # shape (n_sv, n_modes)
        y0 = state_variables[0, :]
        y1 = state_variables[1, :]
        y2 = state_variables[2, :]
        y3 = state_variables[3, :]
        y4 = state_variables[4, :]
        y5 = state_variables[5, :]
        y6 = state_variables[6, :]
        y7 = state_variables[7, :]
        y8 = state_variables[8, :]
        y9 = state_variables[9, :]

        A = self.A
        B = self.B
        G = self.G
        a = self.a
        b = self.b
        g = self.g
        C = self.C
        v0 = self.v0
        e0 = self.e0
        r = self.r
        p = self.p

        # Functions

        def Sigm(v):
            return 2 * e0 / (1 + np.exp(r * (v0 - v)))

        C1 = self.C1
        C2 = self.C2
        C3 = self.C3
        C4 = self.C4
        C5 = self.C5
        C6 = self.C6
        C7 = self.C7

        # Coupling Terms (from coupling array)
        c_glob = coupling[0, :]

        # Derived Variables
        self.lfp = lfp = y1 - y2 - y3

        # Time Derivatives
        # Broadcast every derivative to a common per-node shape so constant
        # (state-independent) derivatives — e.g. ``duA/dt = cA`` — stack into a
        # homogeneous array alongside node-shaped ones, matching TVB's own
        # ``numpy.full_like`` handling of constant drifts.
        _derivs = np.broadcast_arrays(
            np.asarray(y5),  # y0
            np.asarray(y6),  # y1
            np.asarray(y7),  # y2
            np.asarray(y8),  # y3
            np.asarray(y9),  # y4
            np.asarray(
                -y0 * a**2 - 2 * a * y5 + A * a * Sigm(c_glob + y1 - y2 - y3)
            ),  # y5
            np.asarray(
                -y1 * a**2 - 2 * a * y6 + A * a * (p + C2 * Sigm(C1 * y0))
            ),  # y6
            np.asarray(-y2 * b**2 - 2 * b * y7 + B * C4 * b * Sigm(C3 * y0)),  # y7
            np.asarray(
                -y3 * g**2 - 2 * g * y8 + C7 * G * g * Sigm(C5 * y0 - C6 * y4)
            ),  # y8
            np.asarray(-y4 * b**2 - 2 * b * y9 + B * b * Sigm(C3 * y0)),  # y9
        )
        return np.array(_derivs)
